claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi reduces the stacking-fault energy of equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
The reduced stacking-fault energy causes deformation twinning to activate more readily instead of pure dislocation glide under dynamic loading.
Enhanced deformation twinning explains the strength–ductility balance and its temperature and strain-rate dependence relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial FeNiCrMn material is fully homogenized and single-phase.
The initial FeNiCrMn material is equiatomic and in an as-solidified state.
Twin-boundary density is a measurable structural mediator of the proposed deformation response.
Lower temperatures and/or higher strain rates promote deformation twinning in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning contributes to work hardening under the proposed low-temperature or high-strain-rate conditions.
Deformation twinning increases yield strength and ductility under the proposed conditions.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, thermally activated dislocation glide becomes dominant.
Dominance of thermally activated dislocation glide diminishes the mechanical-property difference between FeNiCrMn and CoCrFeMnNi.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, FeNiCrMn will have greater twin density than CoCrFeMnNi.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength than CoCrFeMnNi.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility than CoCrFeMnNi.
At elevated temperatures and lower strain rates, the mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn will converge with that of CoCrFeMnNi.
The hypothesis applies only where both alloys remain homogenized single-phase solid solutions without precipitation or secondary-phase formation.
A matched comparison at 77 K and 300 K over strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1 can distinguish the proposed mechanism.

Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in both twin density and yield strength for FeNiCrMn under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions would falsify the proposed primary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The material is described as both fully homogenized and as-solidified. Homogenization is a post-solidification heat treatment, so an alloy cannot literally be both without clarifying that 'as-solidified' refers only to the production route rather than the tested condition.

The stated test boundary extends only from cryogenic to ambient temperature, whereas the mechanism and prediction invoke high or elevated temperatures. It is unclear whether 'elevated' means ambient temperature or a regime outside the declared boundary.
